Published online:
September 11, 2026

Geographic focus:
Global (primary focus: USA, Japan, India/BRICS, Sweden/Europe, Middle East)

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [NO]
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
A multi-theme weekly markets preview covering five key events: a pivotal Fed rate decision under new Chair Warsh (hike expected but uncertain), a near-certain BOJ hike to 1.25% with focus on what follows, surging commodity prices (Brent >$100, copper at record highs, food inflation risk), a BRICS CBDC payment linkage proposal in New Delhi, and a knife-edge Swedish election with far-right influence implications.

---

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US yields, US interest rates?
Relevance: YES (The Fed decision is the lead story and most market-sensitive thread of the article, though the piece is multi-thematic)

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 75 (Clearly the dominant Fed scenario discussed — a hike is the base case)
Probability of increase: ~60% (Markets lean toward a 25bps hike but "plenty of investors remain unconvinced")

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 40 (Holding is the credible alternative scenario, supported by rates being unchanged throughout 2026)
Probability of holding: ~40% (Meaningful minority view; no consensus lock-in)

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 0 (Not mentioned, not a live scenario given hawkish backdrop)
Probability of decrease: ~0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: +65 (Distinctly hawkish — new Chair Warsh struck a hawkish tone, hot jobs report bolstered hike bets, surging energy/commodity prices add inflationary pressure, and Warsh's deliberate lack of forward guidance amplifies uncertainty to the upside)
